product_brief: World’s first end-to-end PQC-safe, in-flight network encryption solution for Fibre Channel networks.
pqc_capability_description: Hardware-based PQC-safe encryption using LMS Silicon Root of Trust and AES-GCM-256 in-flight encryption algorithms with keys negotiated using ML-DSA-87 and ML-KEM-1024. PQC support for SPDM 1.4 with ML-DSA-87 and ML-KEM-1024.
key_management_model: Session-based, touchless, autonomous; no external key managers, no long-lived keys; each connection independently keyed.
primary_platforms: OEM server platforms, Everpure FlashArray, VMware vSAN, Microsoft Azure Local
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Transparent to all OSs, Fabric, and applications; no switch changes, no external key managers, and no fabric reconfiguration required.
financial_&_business_impact: Lowest Cost; storage array services remain intact.

product_brief: Integrated post-quantum cryptography capabilities for optical networking infrastructure via PacketLight and Quantum XChange partnership.
pqc_capability_description: Integrates NIST-standardized PQC alongside existing Layer-1 encryption and QKD. Supports PQC, QKD, or hybrid combinations. Uses Quantum XChange’s Phio TX® platform for crypto-agility. Targets DWDM and OTN networks.
key_management_model: FIPS-validated cryptographic management platform (Phio TX®) supporting multiple key sources (PQC, QKD)
fips_validated: Yes (PacketLight’s existing Layer-1 encryption is FIPS-certified; Quantum XChange’s Phio TX® is FIPS-validated)

product_brief: Crypto-agile software module providing hybrid post-quantum encrypted communication channels with selectable NIST PQC KEMs.
pqc_capability_description: Uses CryptoQoR™ software to generate, hybridize, and rotate session keys using NIST post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and classic key encapsulation methods (KEM). Provides end-to-end, hybrid post-quantum encrypted communication channels leveraging kernel-based multithreaded encryption protocols. Supports multiple NIST PQC algorithms with user-selectable choices and in situ addition/replacement without equipment replacement.
crypto_primitives: RSA, Elliptic Curve, NIST post-quantum cryptography (PQC), classic key encapsulation methods (KEM)
key_management_model: Generates, hybridizes, and rotates session keys composed of quantum-resistant public-private key pairs; authentication includes quantum-algorithm key material.
architecture_type: Software crypto module; supports Point to Point, Multipoint to Point (EDGE-to-Cloud), and Multipoint to Point (on-premises) topologies.
pqc_roadmap_details: Supports soft-updates with future algorithms as standards are issued; allows in situ addition or replacement of quantum-resistant algorithms without product recall or network interruption.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Supports in situ addition or replacement of algorithms without product recall, equipment replacement, or network interruption.

product_brief: World's first post-quantum secure transport system capable of switching cryptography methods without interrupting communications.
pqc_capability_description: The system uses NTT's proprietary Elastic Key Control technology to flexibly combine multiple cryptography methods, including state-of-the-art post-quantum cryptography. It complies with NIST standards and allows for rapid, secure combination of different cryptography methods and smoother switching without service disruption.
key_management_model: Elastic Key Control technology; two-stage configuration where multiple keys are shared using multiple cryptographic algorithms as key exchange methods, then hybridized to generate a single common key. Key management, session management, and encryption processing are controlled externally via disaggregation from the NOS.
architecture_type: Disaggregated configuration; encryption processing is separated from the Network Operating System (NOS) and integrated into open optical transponders.
primary_platforms: Open optical transponders; IOWN International All-Photonics Network (APN)
pqc_roadmap_details: The system is designed to address the "2030 Cryptography Problem" and supports rapid transition to post-quantum cryptography. It will be utilized on the IOWN international all-photonics network connecting Japan and Taiwan.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Supports crypto-agility allowing rapid updating of cryptographic methods with minimal disruption to service.

product_name: C-DOT Quantum CEM Encryptor (Compact Encryption Module)
product_brief: An 80 Mbps throughput quantum-safe encryptor for IP networks supporting PQC and hybrid key generation.
pqc_capability_description: Supports Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithms under NIST standardization based on Lattice LWE and Code-Based problems. Offers hybrid key generation using PQC, QKD, classical, and static keys. Currently an 80 Mbps throughput device; higher throughput scalable tamper-resistant PQC encryptor is in development.
key_management_model: Hybrid key generation and distribution supporting multiple sources: QKD, PQC, Classical, and static keys.
architecture_type: Hardware encryptor for IP networks; described as a Compact Encryption Module (CEM).
target_industries: Telecommunication, IT, Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI), Government, Military, Utilities, Health and pharmaceutical industry, IoT
pqc_roadmap_details: In process of developing higher throughput scalable tamper-resistant PQC encryptor.
qkd_protocols_&_quantum_networking: Supports integration with QKD for key generation. C-DOT has developed QKD systems based on Distributed Phase Reference (DPR) protocols and is developing Measurement Device-Independent (MDI) QKD.

product_brief: Commercially available QKD systems natively incorporating the latest PQC standard for quantum-safe networking.
pqc_capability_description: Commercially available QKD systems natively incorporate the latest PQC standard. Specifically, they natively use the current NIST PQC Key Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM) standard. QKD keys can be combined with PQC keys and conventional Diffie Hellman keys. This is an option on new systems and a software upgrade for deployed systems. Future NIST PQC algorithms can be easily added.
key_management_model: Hybrid (QKD keys combined with PQC keys and conventional Diffie Hellman keys)
architecture_type: Hardware-based (QKD systems) with software-based PQC integration
pqc_roadmap_details: New PQC algorithms released by NIST in the future can be easily added to the platform.
qkd_protocols_&_quantum_networking: QKD is a hardware-based method using particles of light to distribute secure encryption keys across optical networks. Protocols are proven secure from all computational attacks.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Available as a software upgrade to already deployed systems; easier to simultaneously deploy both QKD and PQC.

product_brief: Integrated ecosystem of applications, computers, network encryption, and cloud for secure, classified, and post-quantum working.
pqc_capability_description: SINA is future-proof and expandable with new features. It includes integrated post-quantum cryptography (PQC) to protect highly classified data against store-now-decrypt-later attacks. The system has been in daily use with post-quantum encryption since 2021.
key_management_model: Hardware-based cryptography; secure key storage implied by hardware security features and separation of virtual working environment from firmware/hardware.
architecture_type: Hardware security product (HSM, smart card, secure element, QRNG, QKD, or semiconductor); includes workstations, rugged crypto clients, multi-crypto phones, and network encryption boxes (L2/L3).
primary_platforms: SINA OS system platform; smartphones, laptops, tablets, rugged devices, network boxes.
target_industries: Government, Public Administration, Defence, Military, Authorities, Municipalities, International Organizations (NATO, EU).
regulatory_status: BSI-approved devices; compliant with German classified information directive (VSA); supports classification levels up to SECRET (German national, NATO, EU).
pqc_roadmap_details: Already working with PQC technologies since 2021; system is future-proof and can be expanded with new features and solutions at any time.
